Battle of Leyte Gulf. Fought from October twenty-third to twenty-sixth, nineteen forty-four in the waters around the Philippine island of Leyte, this battle ranks as the largest naval engagement in history by tonnage and surface area. American forces returning to liberate the Philippines crushed the Japanese fleet in a three-pronged battle that shattered Japan's remaining naval power and confirmed American dominance of the Pacific.

This largest naval battle in history consisted of three distinct engagements—Kurita's Center Force, Nishimura's Southern Force, and Ozawa's Northern Force. Admiral William Halsey commanded the American assault force, while Japanese forces were under Admirals Kurita, Nishimura, and Ozawa. The battle sank or crippled all four Japanese battleships involved, including the massive Yamato, with Japanese losses totaling twenty-six ships.

General Douglas MacArthur fulfilled his promise "I shall return" by landing on Leyte the day the battle began. The victory established U.S. naval superiority as absolute. Japan possessed no fleet capable of organized operations, marking the functional end of Japanese naval combat capability. In desperation, the Japanese deployed kamikaze suicide aircraft tactics for the first time in large numbers. American losses included one light carrier sunk and two escort carriers sunk by air attack, but this represented an overwhelming tactical and strategic victory. The triumph over the Japanese fleet meant that nothing now stood between the Americans and the home islands themselves.
